description: The Etna observatory at the Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia produced reconstructed volcanic deposits and eruption-rate observations for the 6–8 December 2015 New Southeast Crater eruption. The named Zenodo release lists time-averaged discharge-rate and cumulative-volume curves, a pre-eruption digital elevation model, ground-control-point residuals and a deposit-thickness map. The describing article says SEVIRI thermal imagery supplied 15-minute eruption-rate estimates and Pléiades stereo imagery supplied a two-metre pre-eruption DEM over roughly 15 by 15 kilometres around the summit and southeastern flank. Zenodo marks the dataset open under CC BY-NC 4.0; access is free but commercial reuse is limited. A modeller could use the topography, deposit map and flow-rate curve to test lava-flow spread or hazard-exposure scenarios for roads and buildings near Etna. The reconstruction concerns one short eruption and includes derived quantities, not a general probability model of future eruptions. Terrain alignment and assumed material properties affect simulated paths; the article gives uncertainty ranges for volume estimates. The files were not downloaded and the numerical fields were not independently checked. No directly related catalogue dataset was identified.
name: Satellite-based reconstruction of the volcanic deposits during the December 2015 Etna eruption
notes: G4-0536; G4 other data journals. Metadata only. Simulation uses are reviewer assessments. Data payloads and code execution were not checked.
